_meta.purpose: Nano banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image via fal.ai) prompts for labeled-diagram images to power photo-diagram hotspot skills for Grade 10 (Senior School, first Senior School grade). Grade 10 currently has only one subject built as skill files — Music and Dance (web/src/skills/musicAndDanceG10/) — and had zero images of any kind before this batch. Every image and its full part list is sourced directly from curriculum-reference/grade-10/music-and-dance.json and the actual shipped skill files' own content pools, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md and curriculum-reference/RIGOR-STANDARDS.md. Music and Dance is Grade 10's Creative-Arts-family subject, matching the explicit user priority that Creative Arts subjects get a large share of the app's images.
updateLog: 2026-08-29 initial batch: 6 images, all Music and Dance. Chosen after reading every candidate skill file (kenyanIndigenousInstrument.ts, westernMusicalInstruments.ts, kenyanFolkSongsAppreciation.ts, kenyanFolkSongsPerforming.ts, danceProduction.ts, contemporaryDanceFromKenya.ts, classicalMusicMedievalRenaissance.ts) and applying the same test the Grade 9 batch used: propose an image only where a real photograph-style/richly-illustrated image is genuinely better than a code-drawn SVG. Excluded on that basis: kenyanFolkSongsAppreciation.ts (elements of music, expressive devices, performance media — all purely auditory/abstract, no visual object to depict, and the file's own header comment already documents this as a deliberate skip) and classicalMusicMedievalRenaissance.ts (Medieval/Renaissance genres are distinguished by sound and text language, not by any depictable visual difference — an image would either show nothing genre-specific or would have to fabricate a fake visual cue, which RIGOR-STANDARDS.md's honesty discipline rules out; this matches the task brief's explicit instruction to skip purely notational/abstract content). The 6 images that passed: (1) mad-g10-kenyan-indigenous-instruments-gallery — kenyanIndigenousInstrument.ts's own header comment explicitly documents 'no VisualSpec in types.ts fits a specific Kenyan indigenous instrument... a deliberate, documented skip' — the single strongest, author-flagged gap in the whole subject. (2) mad-g10-western-instrument-families-gallery — westernMusicalInstruments.ts has one SVG (string-instrument-diagram) covering only the strings family's structure/parts; brass, woodwind, percussion and piano/organ are real, visually distinct physical objects covered by zero visual branches at all (the file's own comment calls this 'not a visual gap' only because no SVG type exists for them — a real photo-style gallery closes that gap without needing a new SVG type). (3) mad-g10-dance-production-scene — danceProduction.ts's 5 production areas (costumes, props, set design, multimedia, music/lighting/sound) are a themed real-world stage scene, exactly the kind of richly-illustrated content a code-drawn SVG can't represent honestly; the file's own comment documents 'no VisualSpec represents dance elements, costumes, or set design... a deliberate, documented skip.' (4) mad-g10-elements-of-dance-gallery — danceProduction.ts's 5 elements of dance (Body, Action, Space, Time, Energy) are physical/spatial qualities of a dancer's body, best shown as illustrated dancer poses. (5) mad-g10-contemporary-dance-basic-skills-gallery — contemporaryDanceFromKenya.ts's 5 basic performing skills (posture, alignment, balance, coordination, control) are likewise physical dancer-body qualities with no SVG fit, and the file's comment documents the same 'no dedicated VisualSpec... deliberate, documented skip' pattern. (6) mad-g10-kenyan-folk-song-costumes-props-gallery — kenyanFolkSongsPerforming.ts's 'costumes, props and artefacts' choice-factor names real, physical, culturally-specific objects (beaded costumes, gourds, traditional tools) that a real-object gallery represents far better than any abstract diagram; distinct in content from image (3)'s road-safety dance costume/prop content (different sub-strand, different named objects, no overlap).
howToUse: 1. Copy one entry's `prompt` field verbatim into fal.ai (nano banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
2. Save the returned image, then tell Claude which `id` it corresponds to and where the file was saved.

3. Claude will inspect the image with vision to confirm every letter actually printed on the image matches an item in that entry's `expectedLabels`, note (and skip, not guess) any duplicated/ambiguous printed letters, run `npm run images:webp` (from web/) to convert the source PNG to WebP in place, add/reuse an entry in the shared cross-skill registry `web/src/lib/photoImages.ts` (never inline the image/part data directly in a skill file), wire a multi-Bloom's-tier set of question branches into the skill file(s) named in `targetSkillFile` per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, and verify (tsc + lint + a real request against the running dev server) before calling it done.

4. If any part is missing an arrow/letter, or a letter's arrow lands on the wrong structure, regenerate with a corrected prompt (add an explicit correction line naming the missing/misplaced part) rather than accepting a partial image — every part in `expectedLabels` must be identifiable.

5. An image is not tied to the one skill in `targetSkillFile` — once registered in photoImages.ts, reuse it from any other skill (same or different subject, same grade) that has a genuine curriculum reason to reference it, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's photo-diagram section.
_meta.styleGuideSummary: All prompts embed the same style block so every generated image reads as one consistent visual system across the whole app — do not vary the style between images.
_meta.criticalRule: Every prompt instructs nano banana NOT to print any part's name as text anywhere on the image — only a circled capital letter + thin leader line per part. This is deliberate and different from typical stock 'labeled diagram' images (which usually print full text labels): text labels would give the answer away before the question is even asked. If a returned image has any part's name printed as text, it must be regenerated.
_meta.displayConstraint: Confirmed in web/src/components/visuals/Visual.tsx's PhotoDiagram renderer: images display at max-height 420px, max-width 672px (Tailwind max-w-2xl), object-contain, width 100% of container. Source images at roughly 1024-1200px on the long edge are plenty — this is never a print asset. The `dimensions` field on each entry below states the generation aspect ratio/size that best fits that constraint.
_meta.noteNameCaution: Music content risks hotspot letters colliding with note names (C, D, E, F, G, A, B) that appear constantly in this subject's own vocabulary, even though none of these 6 images individually names a pitch. As a subject-wide precaution (per the task brief's hard-won Grade 6 lesson), both instrument-gallery images (1 and 2) deliberately use letters P through V instead of A through G. The 4 dance-content images (3-6) have no note-name content at all, so they use the ordinary A-onward sequence with no risk of collision.
_meta.galleryStyleCaution: Per the task brief's hard-won lesson from the Grade 6 batch, every image below with 4+ separate named items uses a GRID of independently-bordered single-item panels (one instrument/object boxed per panel, its own letter beside its own panel) rather than scattering hotspot letters across one shared busy scene — the one exception is mad-g10-dance-production-scene, which is deliberately a single connected stage scene (not a gallery of separate objects) because its 5 elements are meant to be seen relating to each other within one themed performance, matching the pattern already used successfully for ss-g9-topographical-map-symbols and the rift-valley cross-section in the Grade 9 batch.
